mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an active monetary easing policy that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.25 percentage points over the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 6.0% for two consecutive months, it triggers a policy response that stabilizes the labor market and boosts consumer confidence, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE has been above 6.0% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both the unemployment rate and housing starts signals a strengthening labor market and improving consumer spending, which together drive positive equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where both UNRATE and HOUST decline consecutively for two months.

mechanism_narrative: In a recession marked by a quarterly GDP contraction (GDPC1 decline > 0.5% YoY) and high consumer credit (RSAFS > 350,000 million dollars), the S&P 500 exhibits positive 60-day returns as the market prices in anticipated fiscal stimulus and eventual economic recovery.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods meeting the recession and high credit conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) over the past two months indicates a weakening manufacturing sector, which typically precedes a market correction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO declines for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate falls below 1.0% and remains there for at least one month, it signals an aggressive monetary policy response to the crisis, which is associated with positive equity returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS is below 1.0% for one month.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-unemployment regime (UNRATE > 6.0%) combined with weak housing starts (HOUST < 850,000 units), the S&P 500 tends to decline as the market prices in prolonged economic distress, producing negative 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where UNRATE > 6.0% and HOUST < 850,000.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in consumer credit (RSAFS) over the past month indicates reduced consumer spending, which typically leads to lower corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS declines for one month.
